title: How Many Times a Word Can Be Spelled
statement:
You have a pile of letter tiles, given as the string tiles, and a word. Each tile can be used at most once, and the order of the tiles does not matter.

Return the largest number of complete copies of word you can lay out at the same time.

The classic version of this puzzle always uses the word "balloon"; here the word is an input, so the same code handles any word.

examples.why: There are two b's, two a's, four l's, four o's and two n's: exactly enough for "balloon" twice. The x is unused.
Three b's, but "balloon" needs two l's and two o's per copy, and there are only three of each. Doubled letters must be counted twice per copy.
Two c's, two a's and two t's. The o is left over.

constraints: Both strings contain lowercase English letters
hints: Order does not matter, so only letter counts do.
For each letter of the word, the tiles allow count_in_tiles / count_in_word copies, rounded down.
The answer is the smallest of those ratios: the scarcest letter limits everything.

explain.intuition:
Since tiles can be rearranged freely, a pile is really just a count per letter. One copy of the word uses need[c] tiles of each letter c. Letter c alone would allow floor(have[c] / need[c]) copies, and every letter has to keep up, so the answer is the minimum of those ratios.

It is the same as a recipe: if a cake needs 2 eggs and 3 cups of flour, the ingredient that runs out first decides how many cakes you bake.
steps: For each letter c with need[c] > 0, compute floor(have[c] / need[c]).
Return the minimum of those values.
pitfalls: Ignoring repeated letters in the word. "balloon" needs two l's and two o's per copy.
Taking the minimum over all 26 letters, including ones the word does not use, which forces the answer to 0.
Dividing before checking for a missing letter and getting NaN or an exception from 0 / 0.

solutions.title: Spell copies until a letter runs out
solutions.idea: Count the tiles, then repeatedly take one copy's letters out of the counts until some letter is short.

solutions.title: Minimum ratio of counts
solutions.idea: The scarcest letter, relative to how often the word needs it, limits the number of copies.

followups: You may spell several different words. Maximize the total number of words laid out. Why does greedy fail now?
Tiles include blanks that can stand for any letter. How do you place them?
